title: Connect your web application to Frontend Observability

blocks.content: Use Grafana Cloud Frontend Observability to investigate real user performance, errors, and sessions. You will create an application, install the Faro Web SDK in your own frontend, and check that data arrives. You need permission to create applications and access to your frontend code.

blocks.prompt: What origin serves your website? Include http:// or https:// and a port if needed, without a path.

blocks.content: An application groups the telemetry from one frontend. To create yours, complete the following steps:
Open **Frontend Observability**. Every application you create is listed here, grouped into **Active**, **Stale**, and **No data**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Open the application setup wizard.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.
blocks.tooltip: Use a name that distinguishes this frontend from other applications and environments.
blocks.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.

blocks.content: Set **Allowed origins** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: Use the scheme, hostname, and port your visitors use; add other environments separately.

blocks.content: If your frontend also runs on another origin, use **Add origin**. You can do this later.
blocks.tooltip: List only the origins you intend to monitor; use exact origins for a narrower CORS policy.

blocks.content: Click **Next** to create the application and its collector endpoint.
blocks.tooltip: Creating the application does not send browser data; you must still install and deploy Faro.

blocks.content: Your application now exists with a collector endpoint waiting for data. Nothing is reporting yet, because your frontend doesn't know about it.
To send Frontend Observability its first data, complete the following steps:
Choose **Manual instrumentation** to view the SDK installation instructions.
blocks.tooltip: The other options can help modify your codebase; manual setup lets you choose how to install the SDK.

blocks.content: Choose the installation method that fits your project: **NPM**, **Yarn**, or **CDN**.
blocks.tooltip: Choose CDN when you cannot change the build, for example on a static site or inside a template.

blocks.content: Click **Copy** and follow the instructions for your chosen installation method in your application.
blocks.tooltip: Initialize Faro early so it can capture errors during page startup; deploy the change before checking for data.

blocks.content: Click **Continue** to move on to source maps.
blocks.tooltip: You can finish the wizard now and deploy the SDK afterward.

blocks.content: Once you install and deploy the SDK, visits to your website can start sending sessions and errors to this application.
The next two steps are optional, so this section only shows you what they do. To look at source maps, complete the following steps:

blocks.reftarget: button[data-testid='data-testid Tab 1. Install source map bundler plugin']
blocks.content: Review the bundler plugin instructions if you want readable production stack traces.
blocks.tooltip: There are plugins for Webpack and for Rollup or Vite.

blocks.reftarget: button[data-testid='data-testid Tab 2. Configure source map uploads']
blocks.content: Click **2. Configure source map uploads** to review the upload configuration.
blocks.tooltip: Keep upload credentials in your build environment, never in browser-delivered code.

blocks.content: Click **Continue**. You can set source maps up later from the application settings.
blocks.tooltip: This advances the wizard without requiring a source-map upload.

blocks.content: Source maps are what turn an unreadable production stack trace back into a line in your own code.
The last step offers a set of ready-made alert rules. To finish connecting your application, complete the following steps:
Review the error alert and its threshold. Enable it only if it suits your application.
blocks.tooltip: Check the rule description and notification routing before enabling alerts.

blocks.content: Review the **Web Vitals** alerts to decide which performance signals you want to monitor.
blocks.tooltip: Choose thresholds that suit your users and review them as traffic changes.

blocks.content: Click **Complete** to return to your applications. You can leave the optional alerts off.
blocks.tooltip: An application with no events remains under No data until an instrumented page sends telemetry.

blocks.content: The application is configured. Deploy the Faro SDK, then visit your website and use it to generate browser telemetry.

Open your application and check its own recent sessions and errors. It may remain under **No data** until the first events arrive. If it stays empty, check the collector URL, allowed origin, and browser network errors; data from another application does not confirm this one is connected.
